evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError, with subclasses ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError, is the shared error abstraction used by every entity file
src/domain/task.ts: createTask throws ValidationError and markTaskDone throws ConflictError; TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus are defined only here

src/domain/repositories.ts: TaskFilter.status uses the imported TaskStatus type rather than redefining the status values; UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository are ports built over the entity interfaces
src/domain/project.ts: createProject trims the name and throws ValidationError("Project name is required")
src/domain/user.ts: createUser trims the name and throws ValidationError("User name is required"). This is a similar check to createProject's, but it is this entity's own invariant
All entities (User, Project, Task) follow the same pattern: a readonly interface plus pure functions
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the task-management domain model. It holds the entities (User, Project, Task) with their factory and transition functions, the shared domain error hierarchy, and the repository port interfaces. All three entity files report invariant failures through the module's own error types (ValidationError, ConflictError) rather than throwing plain Error. Each entity keeps its rules in its own file. TaskStatus, TASK_STATUSES and isTaskStatus are defined once in task.ts, and repositories.ts reuses TaskStatus for TaskFilter instead of redefining it. createProject and createUser both trim the name and reject an empty one. This is a small repeated pattern, but each check enforces a different entity's invariant with its own message, so it is not one rule copied into two places. No file uses a different abstraction style: all entities are readonly interfaces with pure factory or transition functions. No file goes around the module's own abstractions.
